nodes.bodyHTML:
Pull request overview

This PR aims to eliminate remaining admit()s in ostd/src by strengthening specs/proofs and adding supporting spec machinery, particularly around frame conversions and page-table mapping preconditions.

Changes:

  • Removed several admit() uses in kspace mapping and frame/segment tracking proofs.
  • Added a FromSpecImpl spec conversion for Frame<M> -> UFrame to connect executable conversions to spec reasoning.
  • Introduced new axioms in ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs to relate UniqueFrameOwner permissions/regions and to construct an owner from a permission.

Reviewed changes

Copilot reviewed 5 out of 5 changed files in this pull request and generated 6 comments.

Show a summary per file
File Description
ostd/src/mm/kspace/kvirt_area.rs Removes admit() around frame->dynframe conversion and mapping preconditions; adds new proof steps to establish mapping requirements.
ostd/src/mm/frame/unique.rs Reworks UniqueFrame::repurpose proof to avoid admit(), leaning on new spec axioms and inner-perm threading.
ostd/src/mm/frame/segment.rs Removes admit() in TrackDrop proof hooks (now empty bodies).
ostd/src/mm/frame/mod.rs Adds FromSpecImpl for spec conversion and strengthens inc_frame_ref_count preconditions; removes a proof admit().
ostd/specs/mm/frame/unique.rs Adds new axioms (owner_from_perm, aligns_with_regions) used to justify UniqueFrame::repurpose proofs.

review_comments.body:
The new `placeholder_slot_perm` + `regions.slots.tracked_insert` introduces an additional `PointsTo<MetaSlot>` for `cur_mapped_pa` while `entry_owner` still carries its own `frame.unwrap().slot_perm` for the same meta slot. Having two independent permissions to the same address breaks the intended linear/unique ownership model and can make the verification unsound. Instead, thread a single slot permission consistently (either move the existing `entry_owner` slot_perm into `regions.slots` before `cursor.map`, or adjust `CursorMut::map`/`item_slot_in_regions` so it uses the slot permission from `EntryOwner` rather than requiring one in `regions.slots`).
```suggestion
                let tracked slot_perm = entry_owner.frame.unwrap().slot_perm;
```

review_comments.body: `map_untracked_frames` now asserts `CursorMut::item_slot_in_regions(item, *regions)` without any proof or precondition guaranteeing `regions.slots.contains_key(frame_to_index(pa))` (which is part of `item_slot_in_regions`). For untracked/device-memory mappings this is generally not true, and previously this was bypassed with `admit()`. Either (a) add/propagate a precondition that the PA range corresponds to tracked meta slots (e.g., `has_safe_slot`/`regions.slots.contains_key` for each mapped `pa`), or (b) refactor `CursorMut::map` so untracked mappings do not require `item_slot_in_regions` (or accept an explicit slot permission token when needed).

review_comments.body:
Adding `owner_from_perm` as a `pub axiom fn` is a very strong assumption: it manufactures a `UniqueFrameOwner` (including an `M::Owner` witness) from only a `PointsTo` + index, and additionally ensures `<M as OwnerOf>::wf(...)` without taking any witness as input. This can easily make proofs unsound for metadata types whose `Owner` is not constructible from the metadata alone. Consider changing this to a `proof fn` that takes an explicit `meta_own: M::Owner` (or other witness) and uses `from_raw_owner`, or at least restrict visibility / tighten the `requires` so the ensured `wf` is justified.
```suggestion
    pub proof fn owner_from_perm(
        perm: PointsTo<MetaSlot, Metadata<M>>,
        index: Ghost<usize>,
        owner: M::Owner,
    ) -> (res: Self)
    requires
        perm.is_init(),
        perm.wf(&perm.inner_perms),
        perm.addr() == meta_addr(index@),
        index@ < max_meta_slots(),
        <M as OwnerOf>::wf(perm.value().metadata, owner),
    ensures
        res.inv(),
        res.meta_perm == perm,
        res.slot_index == index@,
        <M as OwnerOf>::wf(perm.value().metadata, res.meta_own),
    {
        Self::from_raw_owner(owner, index, perm)
    }
```

review_comments.body:
`aligns_with_regions` is introduced as a `pub axiom fn`, but its postcondition (slot_owners inner perms and self_addr match the owner's meta_perm) is essentially the same linkage already captured by `UniqueFrameOwner::global_inv(regions)`.
Prefer expressing this as a lemma/proof derived from `owner.global_inv(regions)` (or requiring `global_inv` at call sites) rather than adding another axiom, to keep the spec surface smaller and reduce verification unsoundness risk.

review_comments.body: This proof mints a `slot_perm` via `EntryOwner::placeholder_slot_perm(...)` and inserts it into `regions.slots` to satisfy `item_slot_in_regions`. `placeholder_slot_perm` is an axiomatically-created permission intended as a temporary placeholder, so using it here effectively bypasses the linear “slot permission” discipline and can make the verification unsound. Instead, thread the real slot permission for `cur_mapped_pa` into this function (e.g., via preconditions/arguments that provide the existing `regions.slots[idx]` permission) or restructure so the `CursorMut::map` precondition is met without fabricating permissions.
